agent_priors_used: General prior (not SPIDER evidence): research agents exhibit path dependence and local-attractor behavior, so an inherited next_question can be locally rational yet globally suboptimal and a cognitive reset is warranted before continuing a flagged lane.

General prior (not SPIDER evidence): a treatment cannot be shown to beat a comparator that already sits at the correctness ceiling, so dynamic range / non-degeneracy must be certified arithmetically before any expensive multi-arm comparison is funded.

General prior (not SPIDER evidence): a prerequisite observed failing identically across lanes should be repaired once at the substrate/control-plane level, not rediscovered as MEASUREMENT_INVALID/design-failure in each lane.

General prior (not SPIDER evidence): serial gating chains make off-path breadth cheap but not free; critical-path lanes should be concentrated and off-path lanes pointed at the highest-value non-gated question or parked, each with an explicit park branch.

General prior (not SPIDER evidence): cache/memory invalidation is harder than population and un-questioned stale knowledge is a correctness hazard, so false-accept-first freshness and repair metrics matter more than coverage.

General prior (not SPIDER evidence): small CPU-quantized language models frequently cannot emit reliable structured actions for multi-step tool/Web use, so endpoint capability must be validated against the actual task before an expensive four-arm benchmark is authorized.
General prior (not SPIDER evidence): shipping verified code through a pinned promotion path rather than copying experiment code prevents drift between the audited carrier and the production kernel.

allocation.question: Can local delta repair, measured on a controlled credential-free multi-node substrate with an independently verifiable local-perturbation surface, repair the inherited knowledge affected by a bounded local change (blast radius 1-3: a changed field, endpoint, transport validator/token, or permission) at repair cost materially below an honest cold re-derivation under identical per-trajectory counters (http_requests + retrieval_calls + verification_calls + repair_attempts), while keeping contamination (incorrectly repaired or falsely accepted items) below a preregistered bound and reporting per-family precision/recall and false-accept, so that C-DELTA-REPAIR's registry next gate (controlled local perturbations with repair cost and contamination bounds) is actually measured rather than re-assumed?
allocation.rationale: The active pre-freeze mandate already targets C-DELTA-REPAIR and remains the globally correct Graph objective: it is the neglected, product-central terminating safety action of the loop (repair/invalidate rather than confidently inherit stale knowledge), its last finalized measurement was MEASUREMENT_INVALID (EXP-GRAPH-36106653880) and its only positive is a bounded single-node result (EXP-GRAPH-36018188168), so the registry next gate is genuinely unmeasured, whereas the inherited local next_question (construct a >=2-anchor D1V population) is a precondition the Codex already indicates is unreachable - the accepted EXP-GRAPH-37992949248 reports a single-anchor, transport-coupled, time-stable D1V population and explicitly PARKS the four-anchor Part II route, so another constructibility probe has low marginal value. The design-stage failure that stalled the mandate is a shared control-plane/model failure, not a scientific objection, so I re-affirm the same scientific objective. cognitive_reset was performed (graph is tunnel-flagged): if graph met today's Codex with no inherited next_question it would not re-probe freshness constructibility but would measure whether localized repair protects inherited knowledge under drift at bounded contamination, because that is the loop's only unmeasured safeguard and is directly product-relevant; that equals the active mandate, which therefore wins on its merits.
